findings.scope: 5.203(a) notice15 days subject to commercial-item exceptions; 5.203(c) noncommercial above simplified-acquisition-threshold response minimum30days. Neither is bid-to-contract or enactment-to-effect duration. Other exceptions apply.
findings.sourceTerms: Federal regulation/government edict, public domain; FAC2026-01 effective2026-03-13.

findings.scope: Eligible individuals, not all residents; an estimated national aggregate, not each eligible person’s enrollment probability or territorial program coverage.
findings.sourceTerms: Federal agency published aggregate report, public domain; FY2022 eligibility/participation estimate, no household records.

findings.finding: U.S. importers bore nearly the full tariff cost through import prices. Retail consumer price, domestic competition and downstream producer effects are separate; no universal consumer pass-through fraction follows. A tariff-for-income-tax swap affects different bases and cannot be assumed revenue-neutral.
findings.sourceTerms: Federal government findings, public domain; 2018–2021 tariff effects, report5405 March2023.

places: States participating in CDC lead surveillance
findings.finding: Reported testing/elevated-level data are not a representative mean for every under6 child. Reference value changed from5 to3.5 micrograms/dL in October2021; a policy threshold is not a mean blood-lead concentration.
findings.sourceTerms: Federal aggregate surveillance methodology/data, public domain; no identifiable health records.

places: NHANES U.S. national population; not state/territory estimates
findings.finding: Blood lead examined participants age1+ in 2017–March2020. A population mean requires age-filtered survey weights and laboratory treatment of censored values; a state value cannot be inferred from national sample records.
findings.sourceTerms: Federal public NHANES documentation; no participant-level records collected; nationally representative survey, not state samples.

findings.finding: GAO reports cost/schedule baseline overruns for a selected nuclear-security portfolio. Their magnitudes are not a best typical-town multiplier; design maturity and technology readiness are separate observed project conditions.
findings.sourceTerms: Federal audit report, public domain. Nuclear-security capital-project portfolio only, not municipal construction.

places: ACS supported municipal/county geographies; territory coverage varies
findings.finding: Read matching city/county versus state geography in the same ACS vintage/table; retain five-year estimate period and margins for small places. Do not carry a state mean into a city as a measured city fact.
findings.sourceTerms: Federal aggregate data, public domain; geography/vintage and margins must be retained.

gaps.scope: typical local delivery/cost overruns and public notice lag
gaps.finding: Federal notice rules are the best legal baseline for covered federal contracts only. No comparable municipal project-cohort delay/overrun distribution or resident-awareness lag was established.

gaps.scope: nonmoney rights loss, privacy costs, polling distance, state lead mean and tax-question effects
gaps.finding: No defensible common numerical estimate. For lead, a national survey mean needs weighted analysis and cannot be replaced by the3.5 reference threshold. For taxes, match the bill’s tax base/rate and incidence rather than invent a question-specific revenue fraction.

termsQuestions: Retail privacy-law study at https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0148296323002394 identified; commercial reuse terms not established. No price-pass-through finding adopted.
interpretation: Aggregate observations calibrate totals; they do not choose an individual actor outcome. Legal rules apply only to the stated jurisdiction and vintage. Missing coverage is not legal permission. No excluded source or real-person name is included.
